reason: Both answers correctly identify confounding, reverse causation/selection, ecological aggregation, exposure denominators, spillovers, and heterogeneity, and both propose credible stepped-wedge or staggered difference-in-differences designs with appropriate robustness checks. B is marginally stronger because it links each inference problem to a concrete design response more systematically, clarifies the mismatch between crash-location deaths and resident population, and adds useful preregistration, power, and follow-up safeguards. A is also excellent but its optional instrumental-variable suggestion is less convincingly justified.
